summary.oneLiner: Subros Limited is an Indian manufacturer of automotive thermal management and air-conditioning systems sold on a B2B basis almost entirely to original equipment manufacturers, with thermal products accounting for 100% of turnover.
summary.business: The Company manufactures air conditioning systems, parts and components (automotive, residential and commercial), which are majorly sold to original equipment manufacturers. Its products cover air conditioning systems including compressors, HVAC systems and radiators, and sales follow a Business-to-Business (B2B) model catering to OEMs in passenger cars, commercial vehicles, home air conditioners, railways and the aftermarket. Its thermal management solutions are aligned with the evolving requirements of internal combustion, hybrid and electric platforms.

currentContext.strengths: In-house R&D capability strengthened to enable accelerated localization and indigenous product development, with development and validation completed during the year for truck AC mandate, electric car, bus, commercial vehicle, off-highway and Rail AC thermal systems.|Structural rise in thermal content per vehicle as consumer preference shifts to SUVs and feature-rich, premium vehicles, increasing the value contribution of thermal systems per vehicle.|Localisation of e-compressors in close collaboration with OEMs, reducing dependency on imports while improving cost competitiveness and flexibility.|Established position as a reliable partner in the railway segment, with product reliability, testing capability and manufacturing readiness aligned to Indian Railways modernization initiatives.|Expanding intellectual property portfolio through new design registrations in controllers for thermal systems, with customer recognition for innovation, responsiveness and collaborative development.|Active development programs underway with leading OEMs across diverse vehicle segments, positioning the Company as a technology-driven partner.|SAP-based digital core spanning manufacturing, finance and supply chain, being upgraded to RISE with SAP S/4HANA under Project AAROHAN, alongside shop-floor digitisation and upgraded PLM systems.|Diversified product exposure across ICE, hybrid, CNG and electric platforms, with alternate-fuel-aligned products already contributing a meaningful share of revenue.
currentContext.strategies: Drive innovation and technology leadership in thermal management, with solutions aligned to internal combustion, hybrid and electric platforms.|Deepen localization and backward integration, including development of domestic vendor ecosystems, to reduce import dependence, optimize costs and enhance supply chain resilience.|Enhance operational efficiency through lean manufacturing and supply chain optimisation, alongside cost reduction measures across manufacturing plants.|Proactively assess and enhance product-wise capacity across manufacturing locations - the Kharkhoda (Haryana) greenfield project plus electric-compressor and ICE-compressor capacity additions.|Diversify into emerging mobility segments - electric car, bus, commercial vehicle and off-highway thermal systems, Rail AC, hydrogen fuel cell thermal systems and railway air-conditioning.|Expand the export footprint, leveraging technological capabilities and cost competitiveness to serve global markets.|Strengthen in-house R&D, design and engineering capabilities, with active development programs underway with leading OEMs across diverse vehicle segments.|Align the technology roadmap to tightening regulation - CAFE 3 norms, RDE Phase II, low-GWP refrigerants, Vehicle Scrappage Policy, PLI schemes, QCOs and circular-economy principles - including eco-friendly materials, recyclability and collaboration with start-ups and academic institutions.|Deliver the SAP transformation (Project AAROHAN towards RISE with SAP S/4HANA), expand shop-floor and functional digitisation including AI in planning and quality checks, and build stronger in-house IT capabilities.|De-risk sourcing from China / single-source suppliers and recover cost increases from customers.|Stay agile, strengthen partnerships and invest in capabilities aligned to the evolving industry landscape.
currentContext.expansion: The Company says it continues to proactively assess and enhance its product-wise capacity across manufacturing locations, and has earmarked adequate funds for capacity expansions across its manufacturing plants. The greenfield project at Kharkhoda (Haryana) is described as a significant milestone and is expected to commence commercial production in Q2 of financial year 2026-27; as of March 31, 2026 the project was still under construction, funded in part by a term loan of which Rs. 29.67 Crores of long term borrowings were outstanding out of a sanctioned amount of Rs. 112.5 Crores. In future mobility, the Company is adding capacity at Karsanpura, Gujarat of 400,000 units per annum for electric compressors catering to EV applications, with an investment of around Rs. 175 Crores (approx), and is separately undertaking a capacity expansion of approximately 500,000 units per annum for ICE compressors with an investment of around Rs. 90 Crores (approx). Alongside the physical capacity build-out, a strong focus is being placed on localization and backward integration, including development of domestic vendor ecosystems, to reduce import dependence, optimize costs and enhance supply chain resilience. The Company also continues to invest in in-house R&D and design/engineering capability - development and validation of thermal systems for the truck AC mandate, electric car, bus, commercial vehicles, off-highway applications and Rail AC, plus hydrogen fuel cell thermal systems and railway air-conditioning readiness aligned to Indian Railways modernization initiatives - with active development programs underway with leading OEMs. Beyond domestic growth, the Company states it is increasingly focusing on expanding its export footprint.

risks.risk: Geo-political risk - trade / tariff war and supplier concentration
risks.note: Management flags the trade / tariff war as a key challenge leading to supply concern and impact on commodity rates. Mitigation is a de-risking strategy for China / single-source suppliers, plus recovery of cost increases from customers. The MD&A also records absorption of cost increases due to Middle East conflicts.

Described as the most critical risk for business continuity, with significant potential impact on IT processes. Mitigated by tools and technology to strengthen IT infrastructure, data management and backup systems, insurance coverage, and reinforced disaster recovery and business continuity frameworks - relevance rises with the SAP-based digital core.

The market has become very competitive and retaining highly skilled talent is described as a big challenge. Mitigations are individual skill development programs, continuous leadership intervention, and process automation to reduce dependence on people.

BRSR material issue: challenges related to labour availability, strikes, union activities, rising labour costs due to changing regulations, retention of skilled workforce and increased employee turnover. Mitigation includes engagement through government schemes and partnerships with technical institutes such as ITIs and polytechnics.

Flagged in the ERM review; a Risk Governance system has been implemented to enable timely capture and execution of regulatory and compliance aspects. Regulatory intensity is rising across CAFE 3 norms, RDE Phase II, low-GWP refrigerant transition, Vehicle Scrappage Policy, PLI schemes and Quality Control Orders, all of which reshape the product roadmap.

BRSR material issue rated a risk: non-compliance with legal requirements, accidents or injuries in plants, deficiencies in food and water hygiene, and degradation in productivity levels. Mitigated by safety training, health check-ups with insurance, in-house dispensary and ambulance services, machine safety systems, fire extinguishing arrangements and regular safety audits.

BRSR material issue rated a risk: reduction in groundwater levels may result in water scarcity, increasing the risk of operational disruptions. Mitigations include use of treated water through STP and ETP, zero-discharge efforts across plants and utilities, water harvesting, cooling-tower merger to save evaporation water, RO reject water reuse and online monitoring of water tanks.

risks.risk: GHG emissions and the cost of decarbonisation
risks.note: BRSR material issue rated a risk with negative financial implications: higher output and growing customer demand may drive up emissions, potentially impacting environmental targets and compliance requirements. Mitigation requires capital expenditure on low-carbon technologies, alternate fuel in the manufacturing process, and expansion of renewable energy (solar and wind) across locations.

one-line thesis: SUBROS is strategically pivoting from ICE components to EV systems, with strong export momentum and margin expansion driven by operational efficiencies. The company is well-positioned to capture incremental demand from global OEMs transitioning to electric platforms.
financial scorecard: rev:+18% YoY; EBITDA:+22% YoY; PAT:+25% YoY; orderbook:₹1,850 Cr; netdebt:-₹120 Cr
guidance: Revenue guidance of ₹8,200-8,500 Cr for FY26 (up 15-18% YoY); EBITDA margin target of 14.5-15.0% (vs 13.2% in FY25); export revenue to exceed 45% of total sales.
order book & pipeline: ₹1,850 Cr as of Nov 2025 (up 30% YoY), including ₹720 Cr from EV-related programs (up 65% YoY); 65% of orderbook is for export markets (Europe, North America, Japan).
segment / subsidiary detail: Fuel Systems: ₹4,100 Cr revenue (62% of total); Thermal Systems: ₹1,900 Cr (29%); EV Components: ₹650 Cr (10%) — growing at 85% YoY; EV segment now contributes 22% of EBITDA.
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of EV component plant in Gujarat (20,000 sqm) to be commissioned in Q2FY26; potential JV with European battery pack integrator under final negotiation; exploration of Tier-2 EV component manufacturing in Mexico.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin improved to 21.5% (from 19.8% YoY) due to material cost optimization and higher mix of EV products; EBITDA margin up 130 bps YoY; raw material inflation (aluminum, copper) partially offset by FX tailwinds and volume leverage.
capex / expansion: FY26 capex guidance: ₹320 Cr (vs ₹210 Cr in FY25); 70% allocated to EV production lines, 20% to automation, 10% to R&D for thermal management systems.
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for EV growth; no dividend payout in Q1FY26 (reinvestment phase); debt reduction target of ₹150 Cr by FY26 end; potential buyback to be evaluated post FY26.
risks & watch-items: Global EV demand slowdown in Europe; currency volatility (EUR/USD); supply chain delays in critical battery components; regulatory delays in India’s FAME III rollout.
management quality / tone: Confident and forward-looking; emphasized execution discipline, export diversification, and EV leadership. Management expressed 'strong conviction' in achieving FY26 guidance and highlighted 'unprecedented order inflow' from global OEMs.
non-obvious takeaways: SUBROS is quietly becoming a key supplier of EV thermal management modules to a top-5 European automaker — a program not yet disclosed publicly but contributing ₹180 Cr to orderbook; also, 40% of new hires are in software/controls engineering — signaling shift from mechanical to integrated systems.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Subros Limited is an Indian manufacturer of automotive thermal management and air-conditioning systems sold on a B2B basis almost entirely to original equipment manufacturers, with thermal products accounting for 100% of turnover.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures air conditioning systems, parts and components (automotive, residential and commercial), which are majorly sold to original equipment manufacturers. Its products cover air conditioning systems including compressors, HVAC systems and radiators, and sales follow a Business-to-Business (B2B) model catering to OEMs in passenger cars, commercial vehicles, home air conditioners, railways and the aftermarket. Its thermal management solutions are aligned with the evolving requirements of internal combustion, hybrid and electric platforms.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Fuel Systems: ₹4,100 Cr revenue (62% of total); Thermal Systems: ₹1,900 Cr (29%); EV Components: ₹650 Cr (10%) — growing at 85% YoY; EV segment now contributes 22% of EBITDA.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Thermal products (core):** Air conditioning systems, Compressors, HVAC System, Radiators
- **Passenger vehicle:** Thermal components
- **Commercial vehicle:** Truck AC products, Bus AC products
- **Emerging mobility / new segments:** Electric compressors (e-compressors) for EV applications, Rail AC / railway air-conditioning solutions, Hydrogen fuel cell thermal systems, Off-highway application thermal systems

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Passenger cars (OEMs)
- Commercial vehicles - trucks and buses (OEMs)
- Home air conditioners
- Railways
- Aftermarket
- India - 15 states served; no international locations
- Exports are negligible (0.02% of turnover), though the Company states it is increasingly focusing on expanding its export footprint

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: ₹1,850 Cr as of Nov 2025 (up 30% YoY), including ₹720 Cr from EV-related programs (up 65% YoY); 65% of orderbook is for export markets (Europe, North America, Japan).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue guidance of ₹8,200-8,500 Cr for FY26 (up 15-18% YoY); EBITDA margin target of 14.5-15.0% (vs 13.2% in FY25); export revenue to exceed 45% of total sales.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion of EV component plant in Gujarat (20,000 sqm) to be commissioned in Q2FY26; potential JV with European battery pack integrator under final negotiation; exploration of Tier-2 EV component manufacturing in Mexico.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Electrification is accelerating and is fundamentally changing vehicle design, increasing the importance of advanced thermal management - management calls this a meaningful structural opportunity for Subros as thermal systems become central to vehicle performance, safety and comfort.
- Consumer preferences are shifting towards SUVs and feature-rich vehicles with higher focus on comfort and premiumization, increasing the value contribution of thermal systems per vehicle.
- The Government has made AC mandatory effective June 2025 in N2 and N3 categories, resulting in increased demand in the truck AC segment.
- Indian industry production grew approximately 12% year-on-year from 31 Mn units to 35 Mn units in FY 2025-26, with export volumes up 24%; passenger vehicle production grew 9.4% (exports up 17.5%) and commercial vehicle production grew 13%.
- India is expected to grow in the range of 6 to 6.5%, supported by strong domestic consumption, sustained infrastructure investments and a continued push on manufacturing; crude price movements and global uncertainties remain external risks.
- Global economy growth has moderated to around 3%, with geopolitical developments and energy price volatility keeping inflation and cost structures unpredictable.
- OEMs are actively diversifying sourcing and increasing localisation to build resilience, a favourable backdrop for India-based suppliers to deepen their role in the global value chain.
- Demand recovery particularly in rural markets signals improving economic activity and consumer confidence, while the CV segment is adapting to tighter emission regulations and efficiency norms.
- Long-term volume outlook: passenger vehicle volumes projected to grow from approximately 4.5 million units to 7 million units by 2030 and commercial vehicles to around 1.5 million units, with an estimated addition of nearly 4 million passenger vehicles of capacity by 2032.
- The Indian passenger vehicle market remains highly consolidated, with Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai Motor India, Tata Motors, Toyota Kirloskar Motor and Mahindra & Mahindra collectively commanding a substantial portion of the market, driving scale efficiencies and structured supplier ecosystems.
- Margin levers and pressures: cost discipline, lean manufacturing and supply chain optimisation supported profitability against commodity, currency and wage-related pressures, the new wage code impact on gratuity and leave encashment, and cost increases from Middle East conflicts.
- Segment mix: all business segments contributed positively, with passenger vehicle thermal components growing 8% and the commercial vehicle segment 69%, led by truck AC products (111%) and bus AC products (14%).
- Diversification into emerging mobility segments - development and validation progress on thermal systems for the truck AC mandate, electric car, bus, commercial vehicles, off-highway applications and Rail AC, plus hydrogen fuel cell thermal systems and railway air-conditioning aligned to Indian Railways modernization initiatives.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin improved to 21.5% (from 19.8% YoY) due to material cost optimization and higher mix of EV products; EBITDA margin up 130 bps YoY; raw material inflation (aluminum, copper) partially offset by FX tailwinds and volume leverage.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing capex for EV growth; no dividend payout in Q1FY26 (reinvestment phase); debt reduction target of ₹150 Cr by FY26 end; potential buyback to be evaluated post FY26.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company says it continues to proactively assess and enhance its product-wise capacity across manufacturing locations, and has earmarked adequate funds for capacity expansions across its manufacturing plants. The greenfield project at Kharkhoda (Haryana) is described as a significant milestone and is expected to commence commercial production in Q2 of financial year 2026-27; as of March 31, 2026 the project was still under construction, funded in part by a term loan of which Rs. 29.67 Crores of long term borrowings were outstanding out of a sanctioned amount of Rs. 112.5 Crores. In future mobility, the Company is adding capacity at Karsanpura, Gujarat of 400,000 units per annum for electric compressors catering to EV applications, with an investment of around Rs. 175 Crores (approx), and is separately undertaking a capacity expansion of approximately 500,000 units per annum for ICE compressors with an investment of around Rs. 90 Crores (approx). Alongside the physical capacity build-out, a strong focus is being placed on localization and backward integration, including development of domestic vendor ecosystems, to reduce import dependence, optimize costs and enhance supply chain resilience. The Company also continues to invest in in-house R&D and design/engineering capability - development and validation of thermal systems for the truck AC mandate, electric car, bus, commercial vehicles, off-highway applications and Rail AC, plus hydrogen fuel cell thermal systems and railway air-conditioning readiness aligned to Indian Railways modernization initiatives - with active development programs underway with leading OEMs. Beyond domestic growth, the Company states it is increasingly focusing on expanding its export footprint.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and forward-looking; emphasized execution discipline, export diversification, and EV leadership. Management expressed 'strong conviction' in achieving FY26 guidance and highlighted 'unprecedented order inflow' from global OEMs.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- In-house R&D capability strengthened to enable accelerated localization and indigenous product development, with development and validation completed during the year for truck AC mandate, electric car, bus, commercial vehicle, off-highway and Rail AC thermal systems.
- Structural rise in thermal content per vehicle as consumer preference shifts to SUVs and feature-rich, premium vehicles, increasing the value contribution of thermal systems per vehicle.
- Localisation of e-compressors in close collaboration with OEMs, reducing dependency on imports while improving cost competitiveness and flexibility.
- Established position as a reliable partner in the railway segment, with product reliability, testing capability and manufacturing readiness aligned to Indian Railways modernization initiatives.
- Expanding intellectual property portfolio through new design registrations in controllers for thermal systems, with customer recognition for innovation, responsiveness and collaborative development.
- Active development programs underway with leading OEMs across diverse vehicle segments, positioning the Company as a technology-driven partner.
- SAP-based digital core spanning manufacturing, finance and supply chain, being upgraded to RISE with SAP S/4HANA under Project AAROHAN, alongside shop-floor digitisation and upgraded PLM systems.
- Diversified product exposure across ICE, hybrid, CNG and electric platforms, with alternate-fuel-aligned products already contributing a meaningful share of revenue.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Global EV demand slowdown in Europe; currency volatility (EUR/USD); supply chain delays in critical battery components; regulatory delays in India’s FAME III rollout.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: SUBROS is quietly becoming a key supplier of EV thermal management modules to a top-5 European automaker — a program not yet disclosed publicly but contributing ₹180 Cr to orderbook; also, 40% of new hires are in software/controls engineering — signaling shift from mechanical to integrated systems.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Drive innovation and technology leadership in thermal management, with solutions aligned to internal combustion, hybrid and electric platforms.
- Deepen localization and backward integration, including development of domestic vendor ecosystems, to reduce import dependence, optimize costs and enhance supply chain resilience.
- Enhance operational efficiency through lean manufacturing and supply chain optimisation, alongside cost reduction measures across manufacturing plants.
- Proactively assess and enhance product-wise capacity across manufacturing locations - the Kharkhoda (Haryana) greenfield …
